title.narrative: Provide comprehensive WASH, Shelter/NFI, and Protection interventions to mitigate morbidity and mortality among children and their families in response to the Sudan crisis

description.narrative: ltpgtHumanitarian needs have worsened across Sudan as conflict continues to rage, causing unprecedented levels of human casualties, food insecurity, displacement, extensive damage to critical infrastructure and facilities, including water and healthcare, the collapse of banking and financial services, frequent interruptions to electricity supply and telecommunication services and widespread looting. The hostilities have triggered a significant deterioration in the humanitarian situation across the country, including in the areas previously not affected by conflict, leaving 24.8 million people in need of humanitarian assistance and protection in 2024 (48% children). Against this backdrop, Save the Children International (SCI), in collaboration with 12 humanitarian partners (50% national partners), will lead three consortiums to respond rapidly and effectively to sudden humanitarian needs across Sudan as follows: ltbrgtWASH Consortium (SCI, LM International -Formerly IAS-, SOS Sahil, Solidarités, and WR). The Consortium seeks to improve access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene knowledge for approximately 317,193 individuals. The WASH strategic response encompasses three key components: (i) Emergency Envelope: This component includes a 48-hour rapid response capability to address urgent WASH needs. Activities under this envelope involve water trucking, distribution of hygiene kits, hygiene promotion, water quality monitoring, waste management, construction of emergency latrines, and quick rehabilitation of water yards and hand pumps (ii) Recovery Activities: The project will rehabilitate water yards and hand pumps. The rehabilitation will include the integration of solar systems to ensure a cost-effective and environmentally sustainable water supply and (iii) Institutional WASH Activities: In response to specific emergencies, such as cholera outbreaks, the project will implement WASH interventions in institutional settings, including health, nutrition, and educational facilities. These interventions will ensure that these institutions are equipped with necessary WASH infrastructure and materials, including water purification systems, excreta disposal facilities, cleaning materials, and solid waste management systems.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtShelter and NFIs Consortium (SCI, ACTED, United Peace Organization (UPO), and SOS Sahel): This project aims to provide immediate and sustainable assistance to the most vulnerable internally displaced persons and host communities, benefiting 78,440 individuals. This project is designed to enhance resilience and support recovery through a comprehensive approach. activities will include distribution of Cash for Shelter for vulnerable integrated and returnees’ households, provision and distribution NFI kits to 4,400 IDP households and 840 vulnerable host community households, training on emergency shelter construction and NFIs distribution processes, among other. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtProtection Consortium (SCI, Nada Elazhar for Disaster Prevention and Sustainable Development (NADA), Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP), CDF, and CAFA.): We aim to reach over 206,000 people. The project will focus on prevention and response to protection risks that affect boys and girls affected by the conflict and displacements by establishing and strengthening community-based structures, awareness campaigns/sessions, provision of MHPSS, case management and referral services, and NFIs/cash. The GBV will focus on prevention and response S/GBV through case management, referral provision of CMR and dignity kit, capacity building of caseworkers, establishing and strengthening women and adolescent centers/groups and supporting its operationsltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThese consortiums will operate under a unified consortium structure outlined in the "Consortium governance and management arrangements"). With our combined, unique expertise and proven track records, we are confident in our ability to deliver the project intervention and respond rapid and effectively to the most affected communities. ltbrgtlt/pgt
